subject.title: fix(autoreview): allow safe Python runtime references

question: Does the autoreview owner approve the proposed Python runtime-reference allowlist as a safe credential-scanning boundary after the unrelated Testbox ownership change is removed?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish the false-positive fix, but deciding which secret-like Python AST shapes may be suppressed is an intentional security policy choice that tests alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve narrow allowlist
options.body: Accept the path-scoped Python expression classifier after splitting the Testbox ownership change and retain the supplied rejection coverage.

options.title: Narrow accepted shapes
options.body: Require a smaller set of runtime-reference forms before merge if any mapping, comment, annotation, SQL-counter, or fallback case is too permissive.

options.title: Keep fail-closed scanning
options.body: Decline source-reference exemptions and accept the downstream false positive to preserve the current scanner boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow allowlist
recommendation.body: Accept the path-scoped Python expression classifier after splitting the Testbox ownership change and retain the supplied rejection coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged commits dominate the credential-scanner and hardening history for the affected script.
